findings.reason: naming `reckon/_mcp_tools.STORAGE_SLOW` as the value the count matches makes the census track the producer if the literal ever moves; second instance of the same defect: §2 says a missing path "under the system temporary directory, which holds the legacy `reckon-worktrees` pool, reads as temporary", but the legacy pool path `Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "reckon-worktrees" / stem` is owned by `_workspace_roots` at `reckon/crew/routing.py:469`, which §2 does not name, so the census re-derives where worktrees live beside the modern `.reckon-worktrees` component (`reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:239`) rather than citing the owner of both locations.
findings.text: §2 counts `storage-slow` tool results but names no owner for the sentinel it matches, while `STORAGE_SLOW = "storage-slow"` at `reckon/_mcp_tools.py:9` (with `StorageSlowResult.error: Literal["storage-slow"] = STORAGE_SLOW`, `reckon/_mcp_tools.py:148`) is that value's single definition; the census would re-spell the literal

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — one module `reckon/mcp_census.py` hides log discovery, JSONL parsing, the signature pattern table, the missing-path worktree classification and the transcript tool-result count behind the single `census(window)` function the doctor block and other callers use.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2 filters tool results on the `storage-slow` literal owned at `reckon/_mcp_tools.py:9` and classifies the legacy worktree pool whose location is owned at `reckon/crew/routing.py:454` without naming either owner.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1614, cli_options 336, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §2 adds one module and one public function to `public_definitions` and states in its own text what it retires ("adds one module … and one public function in it, the census; nothing is retired, because no existing reader counts MCP connections or `storage-slow` results"), adds no command or option, no MCP view and no refusal family.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §2 now cites the mechanisms it extends: `transcript_index`/`TRANSCRIPT_ROOT` and the `promotion_receipts` content-block walk in `reckon/velocity.py`, and `_in_linked_worktree` (`reckon/cli_entry.py:132`) and `_repository_named_by_worktree` (`reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:276`) for the working-directory kind; no existing reader of Claude Code's `mcp-logs-*` trees or of `storage-slow` counts exists to reuse (verified: no `mcp_census`, no `mcp-logs` reader, no `STORAGE_SLOW` consumer in `reckon/*.py`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the census adds the per-cause connection counts and per-tool `storage-slow` counts no reader has; it calls existing owners for its sub-decisions rather than re-deriving them, and it extends `promotion_receipts` by extracting a shared walk rather than adding a parallel transcript reader.
